name: Cursor Local IDE
description: Cursor running as a local-first AI code editor (VS Code fork). A workspace is an open folder/repo on disk. Behavior is shaped by a per-workspace .cursor/rules/*.mdc cascade plus global User Rules; chat/composer history and Agent sessions live in local SQLite, browsable from the sidebar. Cloud agents are a separate product.

identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Account-based but the editor itself is local-first. Sign-in is done from the editor's account icon and supports email+password, GitHub OAuth, Google OAuth, magic link (passwordless), and SAML 2.0 SSO on Teams/Enterprise. Login uses OAuth 2.0 and activates the subscription. MFA is handled by the underlying provider. An account is effectively required to use the AI features (model access is gated by subscription), though the editor's local files and history are stored on-device regardless of which account is signed in.
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: Local editor is single-user per machine, but identity ties into team/org structures. Teams and Enterprise plans add SAML 2.0 SSO (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, OneLogin), SCIM provisioning (Enterprise), admin dashboards for seats, model restrictions, and Privacy Mode enforcement. Collaboration around the workspace is mediated through version control (rules files committed to the repo) and Team Rules pushed from the Cursor dashboard that individual developers cannot disable. There is no real-time concurrent co-editing of a single local Cursor session by multiple users.

workspace_model.workspace_definition: A workspace is a directory/repo opened on disk (inherited from the VS Code workspace model). It maps to a filesystem path; Cursor derives a workspace identifier (hash) from that path and uses it to scope per-workspace storage. It is not required to be a git repo, but rules are intended to be version-controlled within the repo. Each opened folder gets its own workspaceStorage/<hash>/state.vscdb SQLite DB. Because the workspace identity is derived from the path, renaming/moving a project can make prior chats appear 'invisible' until re-mapped.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: Chat/composer sessions (Agent conversations) are scoped to a workspace: each chat ('composer') is tagged with a workspace identifier derived from the workspace path. A user can have many sessions per workspace, listed in the sidebar/Agents window, and can run multiple agents in parallel locally (subject to local resource limits). A global SQLite store indexes the Agent history list across workspaces, but each entry is workspace-tagged. Global User Rules and Memories apply across workspaces; project rules and memories are workspace-scoped.
workspace_model.context_scoping: Workspace-level context: project rules in .cursor/rules/*.mdc, legacy .cursorrules, AGENTS.md (and nested AGENTS.md per directory), indexed/cached codebase data, and auto-generated Memories (project-scoped). Global context: User Rules (Cursor Settings -> Rules) and global preferences applied across all projects. Session-level context: the files attached/referenced and RAG-retrieved code snippets for a given chat. Team Rules are an org-level layer pushed from the dashboard.
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: Rules live in .cursor/rules/ as individual .mdc (Markdown Cursor) files, version-controlled per project. Cascade/merge order: Team Rules -> Project Rules -> User Rules, with all applicable rules merged and earlier sources taking precedence on conflict. Rule activation types are inferred from frontmatter: Always (alwaysApply: true), Auto-Attached (globs match), Agent-Requested (description-based), Manual. Nested AGENTS.md files combine with parent directories, more specific (deeper) instructions taking precedence; for nested .cursorrules, subdirectory rules override conflicting root rules by proximity. Known limitation: .mdc files must sit directly in .cursor/rules/ (flat) -- rules in subfolders of .cursor/rules/ are not reliably auto-triggered. Legacy root .cursorrules is still supported but deprecated in favor of Project Rules / AGENTS.md. No widely-documented hard size cap on individual rule files. [uncertain]
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: Not a bounded-source research assistant. Grounding is the workspace codebase itself: Cursor indexes the open folder and uses RAG to retrieve relevant code at query time, plus any explicitly attached files/@-references. There is no notebook/Space corpus model; the 'corpus' is implicitly the indexed repo on disk.

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Local-first SQLite. Per-workspace state in ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/workspaceStorage/<hash>/state.vscdb (macOS; ~/.config/Cursor on Linux, %APPDATA%\Cursor on Windows), using a single key-value ItemTable (inherited from VS Code). A global store (globalStorage/state.vscdb) uses the cursorDiskKV table where each row is a message 'bubble' keyed as composerData:<composerId> (session metadata) and bubbleId:<composerId>:<bubbleId> (individual messages). Additional store.db files exist under ~/.cursor/chats/. Chat content is stored as JSON inside SQLite (not a vector DB). Storage is essentially local; nothing is retained server-side between requests for the local editor.
persistence_and_history.session_history: Conversations are stored as JSON-in-SQLite, structured around composers (sessions) and bubbles (messages). The Agent/chat history list is browsable from the sidebar (Agents window). Key formats include composer.composerData (current chat list), workbench.panel.aichat.view.aichat.chatdata (legacy), aiService.prompts (prompt history), aiService.generations (older response store). History is local and persists across sessions; there is no built-in vendor retention limit since it lives on the user's disk. Export/portability is not a first-class feature -- it requires third-party tooling that reads the SQLite DBs directly. Renaming/moving a project can orphan chats in the UI because they are keyed by workspace path.
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Two distinct layers. (1) Rules = user-authored, durable instructions stored as files (.cursor/rules/*.mdc, AGENTS.md, User Rules) -- explicit, version-controllable, system-prompt-like. (2) Memories = auto-generated rules derived from chat conversations, project-scoped, auto-managed, kept simple (short preferences). Ephemeral thread state (the live conversation, RAG retrievals, checkpoints) is separate from these durable cross-thread stores. Cursor's built-in Memories are intentionally lightweight; richer long-term memory typically requires MCP servers or workspace rule-file injection patterns.
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: History is browsable per workspace via the sidebar list. There is no documented robust full-text or semantic search across all past sessions natively; the global store indexes the Agent history list. Cross-session knowledge reuse is achieved via auto-generated Memories (carry context forward within a project) and rules files, rather than free-text search of prior chats. Codebase retrieval (RAG over the indexed repo) is the main semantic-retrieval mechanism, not chat-history search. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: Persistent by default -- chat/composer history lives indefinitely in local SQLite until the user deletes it or clears storage. No vendor-imposed TTL on the local editor. Checkpoints (codebase snapshots the agent takes before significant changes) are stored locally and separately from Git, used only for undo. There is no automatic hard-deletion of session history; cleanup is manual (deleting workspaceStorage entries or chats).

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: In-process / on-host execution. The local agent runs in the user's own editor process against the real working directory; tool calls (running tests, file edits, terminal commands) operate directly on the local filesystem and the developer's machine resources. There is no per-session VM/container or ephemeral checkout for the local product -- isolation is only what the OS/user provides. Network access is whatever the local machine has. Cursor 3.2 added local worktrees so agents can work on isolated branches in parallel and merge back, providing filesystem-level (not VM-level) isolation between parallel local agents.
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: For the local editor, environment/machine state is not snapshotted by Cursor -- the environment is simply the developer's machine. The only snapshot-like mechanism is checkpoints, which capture modified-file state during an Agent session for undo (codebase state, not installed packages/env). Filesystem/env snapshot+restore is a Cloud Agent feature, not a local one.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: Supported as a bridge to the separate Cloud product: a local agent session can be pushed to the cloud (e.g. prefixing a message with & or /in-cloud) and a cloud session can be pulled back into the local IDE with all modified files and context preserved. Self-hosting applies to the cloud product, not the local editor.
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: Locally a user can run multiple agents/chats in parallel, surfaced in the unified Agents window; parallel local agents can use worktrees (Cursor 3.2) to isolate branches and merge back. Parallelism is bounded by local machine resources rather than a vendor cap. Subagent fanout limits (up to 10 per user / 50 per team) are documented for the cloud/agents context. [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: Primary trigger surface is the IDE itself (chat/composer/agent panels). A Cursor CLI (cursor-agent) also exists for terminal-driven sessions with resume-by-chat-id. Slack/GitHub/web/mobile triggers belong to the Cloud Agents product; the local editor is the desktop entry point.

implementation.implementation_stack: Built as a VS Code fork (Electron). Auth via OAuth 2.0 (GitHub/Google/email/magic link) and SAML 2.0 SSO + SCIM for orgs. Local persistence in SQLite: per-workspace state.vscdb (ItemTable key-value, inherited from VS Code), global state.vscdb (cursorDiskKV bubble store), and store.db files under ~/.cursor/chats/. Chat payloads stored as JSON within SQLite. Codebase context via indexing + RAG retrieval. Rules engine reads .mdc/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules files with frontmatter-driven activation. Model inference and account/subscription state are served from Cursor's cloud; conversation content stays local for the editor.
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: Cursor Local maps cleanly onto Labmate's workspace_id-scoped model: derive a stable workspace_id (Cursor uses a hash of the path; Labmate could use a repo/project key) and tag every session/conversation document with it -- mirroring how each composer is workspace-tagged. The composer/bubble split (session-metadata row + append-only per-message bubble rows) is a close analog to Labmate's MongoDB long-term session docs (composerData) plus an event stream of messages (bubbles), and Cursor's append-only-within-SQLite pattern validates an append-only message log. The two-tier instruction model -- durable user-authored rules (CLAUDE.md-equivalent) vs. auto-generated project-scoped Memories -- is directly transferable to Labmate's split between user instructions and auto-memory. For history retrieval, note Cursor's weakness: history is browsable but not strongly searchable, and is fragile to workspace-id (path) changes -- Labmate should make workspace_id stable and independent of any display path, and add explicit full-text/semantic search over session docs rather than relying on a path-derived key. Cursor's lack of a TTL (local, persists forever) contrasts with Labmate's Redis-Streams active-state TTL; the lesson is to clearly separate durable long-term session docs (Mongo, no TTL) from ephemeral active-session state (Redis, TTL).
